selected_evidence.requirement: Sudo commands logged with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
selected_evidence.summary: Sudoers drop-in created, validated, and log file shows entries like 'Sep 29 08:29:57 : root : ... COMMAND=/bin/whoami' with TSID

selected_evidence.requirement: Sudo command log entries excluded from general system log
selected_evidence.summary: !syslog set in sudoers; journalctl and /var/log/secure grep for matching commands return no hits

selected_evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot id, sudo logging functioning)
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 636556ce-a308-49cc-b873-62cedb1c077d and confirmed sudo -n whoami logged correctly before reboot
sudo -n systemctl reboot returned exit_code 0 immediately

selected_evidence.requirement: Node polled until command execution available again
selected_evidence.summary: Two timed-out polls followed by successful 'echo up' confirming exec availability restored

selected_evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity (real restart, not just service restart)
selected_evidence.summary: Post-reboot boot_id d403d50f-4d28-4c0a-82a4-2e72d1eeee11 differs from pre-reboot 636556ce-a308-49cc-b873-62cedb1c077d; uptime -s shows new boot time 08:30:08

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required functionality (sudo command logging)
selected_evidence.summary: sudoers config file still present post-reboot, sudo -n whoami/id logged with new TSID entries, reboot command itself appears in the log, and log remains absent from journal/secure

commands.command:
set -Eeuo pipefail
echo "== baseline =="
cat /etc/os-release | head -3
sudo -n true && echo "sudo -n ok"

echo "== writing sudoers drop-in =="
cat <<'EOF' | sudo -n tee /etc/sudoers.d/99-command-logging >/dev/null
Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log"
Defaults log_input, log_output
Defaults !syslog
EOF
sudo -n chmod 0440 /etc/sudoers.d/99-command-logging
sudo -n visudo -cf /etc/sudoers.d/99-command-logging

echo "== precreate log file with sane perms =="
sudo -n touch /var/log/sudo-commands.log
sudo -n chmod 0600 /var/log/sudo-commands.log
sudo -n chown root:root /var/log/sudo-commands.log

echo "== check logrotate / syslog config for sudo, avoid double logging =="
grep -ril "sudo" /etc/rsyslog.d/ 2>/dev/null || echo "no rsyslog sudo-specific rules"

echo "== verification: run a benign sudo command =="
sudo -n whoami
sudo -n id

echo "== log file contents =="
sudo -n cat /var/log/sudo-commands.log

echo "== confirm NOT in general system log (journal since boot, last 20 sudo lines) =="
sudo -n journalctl -q --no-pager | grep -i "sudo-commands\|COMMAND=.*whoami" | tail -5 || echo "no matching lines in journal (expected)"
sudo -n grep -i "whoami" /var/log/secure 2>/dev/null | tail -5 || echo "no matching lines in /var/log/secure (expected)"
